6:11 — It’s important to add that Panama, distant and separated from the rest of Colombia, had a significant autonomist/separatist movement that attempted to break away at least four times before 1903, and even briefly succeeded once. In 1855, Panama became an autonomous state within Colombia, with its own constitution and government. The United States showed little interest in these earlier movements until 1903, when Colombia’s government rejected the treaty to build the Canal and the US conveniently switched sides to support Panama’s separation.

The 1903 Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty, signed without Panamanian participation, sparked immediate controversy. The struggle to overturn it and reclaim sovereignty over the Canal Zone lasted nearly 70 years. Demonstrations, angry letters, and even armed clashes eventually led to the Torrijos–Carter Treaties of 1977 and the transfer of the Canal to Panama on December 31, 1999.
